title: The Salt Provision
premise: Ulyana Okonkwo, a storm chaser deep in debt to the Optimists—a cheerful, ruthless lending syndicate—takes one last paid job: resupplying an expedition upriver that has gone silent. Following the river toward its forbidden source before monsoon season, she gathers a ragtag crew who become the family she never chose to want. At the source she finds the expedition alive but guarding a discovery the Optimists will kill to own: salt springs that could break the region's water monopoly. Ulyana must choose between paying her debt with their secret or burning her old life down—and in the end she broadcasts the truth, scatters the debt, and stays, finally measuring life in years.
about_author: Xanthe Nakamura is a former hydrologist turned novelist who has canoed four of the world's great river systems and writes about people who run from home until home runs after them. She lives in a converted boathouse with two dogs and an unhealthy respect for weather.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Chasing a storm across the flats to outrun her debts, she is intercepted by the Optimists' smiling enforcer, who offers a clean slate for one job: find the missing Meridian Expedition upriver. She accepts because running costs more than staying. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking fear of being known.

chapters.title: The Crew Nobody Chose
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the river town of Lowmark she assembles a boat and a crew of misfits: disgraced cartographer Teo, ex-Optimist bookkeeper Sefa, and teenage deckhand Pirro who stows away. Their first night together cracks her armor slightly. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness toward strangers.

chapters.title: Dead Air on Channel Nine
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The last coordinates lead to an abandoned camp—tents intact, radio smashed, a journal page about 'singing water.' First signs someone else is following them upstream. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; the mission becomes personal.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Teo's POV. A rapids wreck nearly drowns Pirro; Ulyana saves him and admits, in fragments, why she left home twelve years ago. Teo maps the river's impossible behavior—the current flows wrong above the gorge. Emotional beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: The Smiling Wake
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The Optimists' second boat appears behind them; Sefa recognizes the enforcer aboard as the man who trained her. A tense parley at a trading post ends in theft of their fuel. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by old allegiances.

chapters.title: Salt on the Wind
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Above the gorge they find the expedition—alive, half-starved, led by Dr. Imara Voss, who refuses to turn back. The source is real: salt springs feeding every river below, guarded by a valley community that fled the Optimists' water monopoly. Emotional beat: awe colliding with suspicion.

chapters.title: The Price of Silence
chapters.summary: Imara's POV. Flashback chapters within: how the expedition discovered the springs and why Voss went silent—she was offered wealth to bury it. Now she asks Ulyana to help seal the valley forever. Monsoon clouds gather on the horizon. Emotional beat: duty versus conscience made flesh.

chapters.title: Two Boats, One Truth
chapters.summary: Pirro's POV. The Optimists arrive; a standoff in the valley turns violent when Sefa defects back to her old masters—or seems to. Pirro steals the syndicate's radio and transmits the springs' location to every town downstream. Emotional beat: a child's courage forcing the adults' hands.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The storm hits as the valley floods; Ulyana and the enforcer fight in rising water over the only evidence ledger. Sefa's double-cross is revealed as a triple-cross—she saved the original survey data all along. The enforcer is swept away; the truth is already loose. Emotional beat: chaos as catharsis.

chapters.title: The Source Is Downstream
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Aftermath: the monopoly collapses as towns tap the truth; the Optimists dissolve into litigation. Ulyana tears up her debt contract on camera, then chooses not to chase the next storm. She plants roots in the valley with her crew. Emotional beat: stillness earned—she measures life in years at last.
